gaps: The plan does not define what happens when FORGE_EXECUTOR changes during an active task, although the accepted decision allows a per-machine environment override (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20-22). Close currently finds a successful companion launch independently of executor mode (factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1833-1860). Specify which writer record remains valid after a switch and test that an old-mode record cannot satisfy the new mode by itself.

The proposed executor field has no declared type in the delegation schema, and the validator permits extra fields (factory/schemas/delegation.json:20-43; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:2555-2582). The plan must bind and validate that field wherever a Claude preparation is admitted; the schema file is outside the task's write scope (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/decomposition.json:19-40).

The fresh Claude cold-reader handoff lacks an executable host and recorder contract. The current grill emits a Codex `spawn_agent` descriptor (factory/scripts/forge_cli/grill.py:523-546), while the recorder requires a prepared `agent_type: griller` row (factory/scripts/record_grill_from_json.py:386-396). The plan says to use a Claude subagent instead but leaves its dispatch, fresh-reader check, and result binding for the implementer to guess (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/task-plans/EXEC-MODES.md:62-63).

The ordinary next-action flow will treat a prepared Claude writer as `inspect-delegate`, because it recognizes only a successful terminal companion launch as completed work (factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:5602-5615,5633-5650). That action tells the operator to inspect registered output (factory/scripts/forge_cli/phase.py:654-664). The plan neither defines the Claude preparation's next state nor scopes phase.py for corrected guidance.

The documentation scope leaves binding instructions that still require a Codex companion and Codex cold reader in every Claude session (AGENTS.md:25,93; factory/skills/forge.md:37-43,157). Neither file is in the 21-path write scope (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/decomposition.json:19-40), so the promised Claude-only workflow would ship with contradictory operating instructions. Adding these and the delegation schema also exceeds the stated 22-file review budget (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/decomposition.json:139-142); reconcile scope and task size.
contradictions: The task plan says default hybrid refuses Claude product edits and defers gated Claude writing until later (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/task-plans/EXEC-MODES.md:8-12,27). Accepted Decision 0085 permits the Claude session to execute through the same gates in hybrid (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:24-26), and the approved story plan explicitly assigns that behavior to this task (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:59-65). The task drops an approved capability.

The recorded criterion says protected markers stay refused for Claude writers (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/decomposition.json:13), but the task plan proposes reusing the native marker checks (.factory/stories/FORGE-WARM-1/task-plans/EXEC-MODES.md:55-58). The current native path exempts the repo-kind marker from protected-state denial and can admit it under an active task scope (factory/scripts/pre_tool_use.py:227-234,1782-1814). Reuse alone does not establish the promised refusal.
resolutions: The write proof must match the current mode; a task begun under another mode is delegated again after a switch (technical notes: Mode switch).
executor is declared in the delegation schema (hybrid|codex|claude) and validated at admission; the schema joins via an approved scope amendment.

Claude cold-reader handoff specified exactly: fresh general-purpose Claude subagent given only the prepared brief, recorded with --cold-result --preparation-id against the existing griller preparation row.
forge next gets a claude-mode next action (edit inside scope, then task close); phase.py joins via an approved scope amendment.
AGENTS.md and factory/skills/forge.md name the three modes; they join via an approved scope amendment within the review budget.
Owner decision (native question, 2026-09-24): hybrid per-task Claude writes are split out and deferred as D-0044; decision 0085 stands.
Protected markers, including the repo-kind marker, are always refused on the Claude path (no native exemption).

artifact_delta.final:
- Mode switch: the write proof must match the CURRENT mode — claude mode accepts only a preparation
  recorded with `executor: "claude"`; hybrid/codex accept only a companion launch. A task begun under
  another mode is delegated again after a switch.
- Protected markers (including the repo-kind marker) are always refused on the Claude path; it does not
  inherit the native path's marker exemption.
- Claude cold reader: grill prepares its usual host-native `agent_type: griller` row; in claude mode the
  handoff reads "run a fresh Claude subagent (general-purpose) with the prepared brief as its only
  input, then record its JSON with `record_grill_from_json.py --gate task --task <id> --cold-result
  <file> --preparation-id <id>`" instead of the `spawn_agent` descriptor.
- `forge next`: in claude mode a Claude writer preparation's next action is "edit inside the task
  scope, then `forge task close <id>`".
- The `executor` field is declared in `factory/schemas/delegation.json` (values hybrid|codex|claude)
  and validated wherever a Claude preparation is admitted. The schema, `forge_cli/phase.py`, AGENTS.md
  and `factory/skills/forge.md` are added through an approved scope amendment at implementation.
- Hybrid Claude writes (decision 0085) are deferred by the owner's decision as D-0044.

current_flow: Claude-coordinated sessions deny Claude product writes; forge delegate launches the Codex companion and close requires a successful companion launch; native Codex coordination uses host-native preparation rows.
summary: Cold read of the simplified task (5 gaps, 2 contradictions), all repository-answerable; contract and task plan amended once.
